# Pubrica

> Research, writing and publication support for science. Medical and regulatory writing, biostatistics, systematic review, scientific editing, translation and publication support for researchers, universities, publishers and the life-science industry. A trading name of Guires, registered in England and Wales and in India, working since 2009.

Pubrica works to the standard each piece of work is judged against: CONSORT 2025, PRISMA 2020, STROBE, ICMJE, GPP 2022, ICH, EU MDR and IVDR, CDISC, and WCAG 2.2. The company holds ISO 9001:2015 (cert. H3CR9TCU20251212INDQM10N). Pubrica does not ghostwrite: the authors are always the client.

## Start here
- [Research, Writing and Publication Support](https://pubrica.com/): Medical writing, statistics, editing, peer review and publication support for researchers, universities and life-science teams. Since 2009.
- [How It Works](https://pubrica.com/how-it-works/): How a Pubrica project runs: scoping, subject-expert allocation, drafting, review and journal submission, with a date we commit to.
- [Pricing](https://pubrica.com/pricing/): Indicative prices with turnaround for manuscript writing, editing, statistical analysis and pre-submission review. Per-word bands, no hidden add-ons.
- [Pubrica Academy](https://pubrica.com/academy/): Free guidance on writing a paper, appraising one, interpreting an analysis and satisfying journal, university and funder rules.
- [Pubrica Insights](https://pubrica.com/insights/): What we did and what changed: real deliverables with the working shown, funder, university and publisher rule changes.
- [12 Free Research Tools, No Sign-Up](https://pubrica.com/free-tools/): Twelve calculators and checkers that run in your browser: sample size, effect size, NNT, heterogeneity, test chooser. No sign-up, no email.
- [About Pubrica](https://pubrica.com/about-us/): Pubrica is a research, writing and publication support company founded in 2009 — 150+ subject experts, ISO 9001:2015 certified, working to COPE and ICMJE.
- [Compliance](https://pubrica.com/compliance/): The ISO 9001:2015 certificate Pubrica holds, the publication ethics codes we follow. Pubrica works to the publication, regulatory and accessibility standards.
- [Contact Pubrica](https://pubrica.com/contact-us/): Reach Pubrica by email or phone in India and the United States. What happens after you get in touch is a scoping read, not a sales call.

## Services
- [Editorial & Journal Services](https://pubrica.com/services/academic-editorial-services/): Editorial office support, copy editing, proof-stage proofreading, indexing, reference and metadata validation, integrity cases.
- [Compliance Statement Checking](https://pubrica.com/services/academic-editorial-services/compliance-statement-checking/): Every submission checked for the statements it must carry — ethics approval, consent, conflicts of interest, funding, data availability.
- [Development Editing Services](https://pubrica.com/services/academic-editorial-services/development-editing-service/): Developmental editing for manuscripts that are sound but not yet readable as an argument. Enhance clarity and improve your manuscript with expert development.
- [Editorial Office and Peer Review Management](https://pubrica.com/services/academic-editorial-services/editorial-office-services/): Peer review operations run in your own system — triage, reviewer identification and chasing, decision letter preparation and author correspondence.
- [Forensic & Quality Audit Services](https://pubrica.com/services/academic-editorial-services/forensic-and-quality-audit-service/): Data integrity, image forensics, plagiarism and authorship, statistical method and compliance against COPE, ICMJE, CONSORT, PRISMA and ARRIVE.
- [Back-of-Book Indexing Services](https://pubrica.com/services/academic-editorial-services/indexing/): Back-of-book indexes built by people who read the book — concepts indexed rather than words counted, with cross-references.
- [Journal Indexing Applications](https://pubrica.com/services/academic-editorial-services/journal-indexing-applications/): Indexing applications prepared properly — the criteria assessed honestly first, the gaps closed. Most indexing applications fail on things the journal could.
- [Research Metadata Tagging](https://pubrica.com/services/academic-editorial-services/metadata-tagging/): Affiliation, contributor, funder and subject metadata applied properly — ROR identifiers, CRediT roles, ORCID and MeSH terms.
- [Permission & Metadata Services](https://pubrica.com/services/academic-editorial-services/permission-and-metadata-services/): Permissions secured for third-party figures, tables and text, licences chosen, and metadata built for PubMed, Crossref, Scopus and DOAJ.
- [Proof-Stage Proofreading](https://pubrica.com/services/academic-editorial-services/proof-stage-proofreading/): Reading the typeset proof against the copyedited manuscript — typographical errors, bad breaks, transposed panels.
- [Reference Validation and Linking](https://pubrica.com/services/academic-editorial-services/reference-validation/): Every reference checked against the source record, DOIs resolved and linked, retracted and withdrawn citations flagged.
- [Research Integrity Case Handling](https://pubrica.com/services/academic-editorial-services/research-integrity-cases/): Integrity concerns investigated and documented to COPE process. Getting the category wrong means publishing a second notice about the first one.
- [Revisioning & Localisation Services](https://pubrica.com/services/academic-editorial-services/revisioning-and-localisation-service/): Manuscripts revised for clarity and logic, then localised for the linguistic, cultural and disciplinary context of the journal or region you are writing for.
- [Scientific Alt Text Writing](https://pubrica.com/services/academic-editorial-services/scientific-alt-text/): Alt text for Kaplan–Meier curves, forest plots, flow diagrams and multi-panel figures. "Chart showing results" is not alt text. Automated alt text can.
- [PRESS Peer Review of Search Strategies](https://pubrica.com/services/academic-editorial-services/search-strategy-peer-review/): Search strategies peer reviewed against the PRESS 2015 guideline — six elements checked line by line, before the search runs or before the paper is.
- [Statistical Review Service](https://pubrica.com/services/academic-editorial-services/statistical-review/): A statistician reads the methods and the results — design, analysis, multiplicity, unit of analysis and reporting.
- [Visual & Accessibility Editing Services](https://pubrica.com/services/academic-editorial-services/visual-and-accessibility-editing-services/): Figures, tables, layouts and PDFs edited to global accessibility standards — alt text, colour contrast, heading hierarchy and tagged PDFs.
- [Accessibility Services](https://pubrica.com/services/accessibility-compliance/): WCAG 2.2 and EN 301 549 audits, VPAT and accessibility conformance reports, PDF and EPUB remediation, MathML, scientific alt text and digital production QA.
- [Data and Artificial Intelligence](https://pubrica.com/services/across-everything/): Statistics, bioinformatics, predictive models and real-world data analysis, with the code and working files handed over so your team can run it again.
- [Bioinformatics and NGS Data Analysis](https://pubrica.com/services/bioinformatics/): NGS analysis with the reference build, tool versions and code recorded: RNA-seq, single-cell, variant calling, proteomics. From $100 a sample.
- [CME Content Development Services](https://pubrica.com/services/continuing-medical-education-cme-content-development/): Needs assessments, modules, assessment items and Standards evidence for accredited providers — written to the five ACCME Standards and EACCME 3.0.
- [Data, Analytics and AI](https://pubrica.com/services/data-analytics-machine-learning/): Predictive modelling, algorithm development, segmentation, patient journey analytics, interpretation and visualisation.
- [Algorithm Development, Training & Optimisation](https://pubrica.com/services/data-analytics-machine-learning/algorithm-development-for-training-and-optimisation/): Custom AI, machine learning, deep learning and optimisation algorithms for healthcare, life sciences and pharma.
- [Customer & Patient Segmentation](https://pubrica.com/services/data-analytics-machine-learning/customer-segmentation/): Segmentation for healthcare, pharma, medical devices and publishing. Tailored insights for targeted research, marketing and publication strategy.
- [Health Economics & Outcomes Research](https://pubrica.com/services/data-analytics-machine-learning/health-economics-outcome-research/): Cost-effectiveness and budget impact models, real-world evidence, patient-reported outcomes and HTA dossiers.
- [Interpretation, Reporting & Visualisation](https://pubrica.com/services/data-analytics-machine-learning/interpretation-reporting-and-visualisation/): Statistical output turned into interpretation a reader can follow, reports built to CONSORT, PRISMA, STROBE and TRIPOD.
- [Patient Journey & Insights](https://pubrica.com/services/data-analytics-machine-learning/patient-journey-insights-machine-learning/): Real-world care pathways reconstructed from EHR, claims, wearables and patient-reported data.
- [Predictive Analytics Services](https://pubrica.com/services/data-analytics-machine-learning/predictive-analytics/): Regression, classification, time-series and survival models for research, clinical and operational questions.
- [Thought Leadership Content and Editorial Design](https://pubrica.com/services/data-analytics-machine-learning/thought-leadership-content-editorial-design/): Executive reports, white papers, bylined articles and editorial design for healthcare and life sciences — with the framework that actually governs each.
- [Editing and Translation Services](https://pubrica.com/services/editing-and-translation/): Proofreading $0.025 to translation $0.12 a word, every rate inside a published band. ISO 17100, ISO 18587 and the reporting guideline your design requires.
- [Book Editing Services](https://pubrica.com/services/editing-and-translation/book-editing/): Scholarly book editing with a personalised list of 3–5 publishers, a proposal per press, indexing and permissions. $0.021 a word at 80,000 words.
- [Manuscript Editing Services](https://pubrica.com/services/editing-and-translation/manuscript-editing/): Copyediting plus formatting to one named journal — its own deviations, the word limit, the figures and the submission checklist. From $500.
- [Post-Editing Services](https://pubrica.com/services/editing-and-translation/post-editing/): Human post-editing of machine and AI translation to ISO 18587. Full post-editing $0.06 a word, light $0.035. Free provenance triage before you buy.
- [Proofreading Services](https://pubrica.com/services/editing-and-translation/proofreading/): Academic and scientific proofreading at $0.025 a word, inside the EFA published band. Precision proofreading for researchers and academics — English.
- [Scientific Editing Services](https://pubrica.com/services/editing-and-translation/scientific-editing/): Manuscript editing read against the reporting guideline your design requires, at its current version. Three editors. From $0.035 a word. Free guideline check.
- [Thesis Editing & Proofreading](https://pubrica.com/services/editing-and-translation/thesis-editing/): Thesis copyediting and proofreading bounded by the IPEd guidelines, July 2025. Structural issues noted, never rewritten.
- [Translation with Editing](https://pubrica.com/services/editing-and-translation/translation-with-editing/): Research translation with independent revision by a second linguist, built to the ISO 17100 structure. $0.12 a word, from $240. 500 words translated free.
- [AI-Assisted Manuscript Editing](https://pubrica.com/services/editing-translation/ai-assisted-manuscript-editing/): For manuscripts drafted or heavily edited with AI — citations verified, overstated claims pulled back, homogenised prose restored.
- [LaTeX Editing Service](https://pubrica.com/services/editing-translation/latex-editing/): Manuscripts edited in LaTeX source — equations, macros, BibTeX and journal class files left working. Most editing services will take your LaTeX and hand back.

- [What is research design? Types, methods and best](https://pubrica.com/services/physician-writing-services/research-proposal/research-design-types-methods-best-practices/): Research design is the plan that decides how data will be collected, analysed and interpreted — and, before any of that, what the study is allowed to.

- [Post-Acceptance Support](https://pubrica.com/services/publication-support/post-acceptance-support/): The work between acceptance and publication — proof correction, author queries, licence choice, funder deposit, metadata and corrections.

- [Response to Reviewer Comments Service](https://pubrica.com/services/publication-support/responding-to-reviewers/): Point-by-point responses and rebuttal letters: every comment triaged concede, answer or decline, with each revision tracked to the manuscript.
- [Resubmission Support](https://pubrica.com/services/publication-support/resubmission-support/): What to do after a rejection — why it was rejected, whether to appeal, transfer or resubmit elsewhere, and the manuscript reworked for the next journal.

- [Scientific Illustration](https://pubrica.com/services/research-impact/scientific-illustration/): Mechanism diagrams, anatomical and molecular figures, device and technique illustration. This is drawing, not reformatting.

## Therapy areas
- [Therapeutic Areas](https://pubrica.com/therapeutics/): Therapeutic-area expertise across oncology, cardiology, neurology, endocrinology, infectious disease, public health and medical devices.
- [Cardiovascular](https://pubrica.com/therapeutics/cardiovascular/): CONSORT 2025 trial reporting, cardiovascular outcome trials that run for years, and registry analyses where device and medicine.
- [Dermatology](https://pubrica.com/therapeutics/dermatology/): Lesion scoring, photographic evidence standards and topical formulation studies, where the assessor can usually see the treatment.
- [Endocrinology & diabetes](https://pubrica.com/therapeutics/endocrinology-diabetes/): Metabolic cohorts, glycaemic endpoints, and cardiovascular outcome trials that exist because a regulator asked for. One named lead across the programme.
- [Gastroenterology & hepatology](https://pubrica.com/therapeutics/gastroenterology-hepatology/): Endoscopic scoring, fibrosis endpoints and microbiome study design, with surrogate endpoints under active regulatory. One named lead across the programme.
- [Immunology & inflammation](https://pubrica.com/therapeutics/immunology-inflammation/): Biologic comparability, immunogenicity reporting and mechanism-of-action writing that has to satisfy an assessor rather than a.
- [Infectious disease & vaccines](https://pubrica.com/therapeutics/infectious-disease-vaccines/): Transmission modelling, efficacy reporting and public-health evidence, in an area where the evidence is read outside the literature as well as inside.
- [Musculoskeletal](https://pubrica.com/therapeutics/musculoskeletal/): Patient-reported outcomes, orthopaedic device evidence and surgical case series, where the intervention and the operator are hard to.
- [Nephrology & urology](https://pubrica.com/therapeutics/nephrology-urology/): eGFR endpoints, dialysis cohort analysis and renal outcome reporting, where competing risks are. One named lead across the programme.
- [Neurology](https://pubrica.com/therapeutics/neurology/): Imaging endpoints, disability scales and longitudinal cohorts, where the measure chosen decides what can be claimed and for how.
- [Oncology & haematology](https://pubrica.com/therapeutics/oncology-haematology/): RECIST and iRECIST reporting, survival analysis, and submission to high-impact oncology journals and regulators who have seen every version of the.
- [Ophthalmology](https://pubrica.com/therapeutics/ophthalmology/): Visual-acuity endpoints, imaging integrity and device evaluation, with a strong overlap into medical devices and. One named lead across the programme.
- [Paediatrics](https://pubrica.com/therapeutics/paediatrics/): Age-appropriate endpoints, assent documentation and paediatric investigation plans, with obligations that begin earlier than teams.
- [Psychiatry & mental health](https://pubrica.com/therapeutics/psychiatry-mental-health/): Rating-scale validation, blinding that is genuinely hard to maintain, and outcomes reported by the person being. One named lead across the programme.
- [Rare disease](https://pubrica.com/therapeutics/rare-disease/): Small-population designs, natural-history studies and orphan designation dossiers, where the usual evidence hierarchy is not.
- [Respiratory](https://pubrica.com/therapeutics/respiratory/): Spirometry endpoints, inhaled device studies and exacerbation-rate analysis, where the device and the molecule are assessed.
- [Women’s health](https://pubrica.com/therapeutics/womens-health/): Trials and registry work in obstetrics and gynaecology, where the therapy area decides the endpoint, the comparator and the reporting checklist.

## Industries
- [Industries We Serve](https://pubrica.com/industries/): Twelve regulated sectors and the standard each is judged against: ICH for medicines, MDR and IVDR for devices, CHEERS for payers.
- [Biologics and Biosimilars Regulatory Writing](https://pubrica.com/industries/biologics/): Comparability and immunogenicity reporting, Module 2 overviews and biosimilar applications written to ICH Q5E and the EMA and FDA biosimilar guidance.
- [CRO Medical Writing and Programming](https://pubrica.com/industries/cro/): Overflow capacity under your sponsor’s quality system: study reports, patient narratives, CDISC SDTM and ADaM.
- [IVD Performance Evaluation and Diagnostic Accuracy](https://pubrica.com/industries/diagnostics/): Performance evaluation plans and reports under IVDR, scientific validity reports, STARD accuracy studies and TRIPOD+AI model reporting.
- [Engineering and Health Technology Writing](https://pubrica.com/industries/engineering/): Algorithm validation reporting, TRIPOD+AI model reporting, technical papers and health technology evidence written for the reader who decides.
- [Generic and Abridged Dossier Writing](https://pubrica.com/industries/generics/): Bioequivalence reports, ANDA and abridged dossiers, literature-based submissions with reproducible searches, and labelling tracked to the reference product.
- [Research Support for Hospitals](https://pubrica.com/industries/healthcare-providers/): Case reports, registry and outcomes analysis, service evaluation and manuscripts, assigned by specialty and built around clinical sessions.
- [Life Sciences and Biotech Writing](https://pubrica.com/industries/life-sciences/): Manuscripts, grants, preclinical reports and omics analysis delivered with the code, reported to ARRIVE 2.0, STROBE or TRIPOD+AI as the design requires.
- [Medical Device Clinical Evaluation](https://pubrica.com/industries/medical-device/): CEP, CER, state of the art review, GSPR checklist, PMCF and SSCP under EU MDR, plus 510(k) technical documentation for the US route.
- [Health Claim Substantiation and Novel Food](https://pubrica.com/industries/nutraceuticals/): Article 13.5 and 14 health claim dossiers, novel food applications and substantiation files built to EFSA guidance under food law, not medicines law.
- [Pharmaceutical Medical and Regulatory Writing](https://pubrica.com/industries/pharmaceutical/): Protocols, statistical analysis plans, ICH E3 study reports, CTD Modules 2.4 to 2.7, health-authority responses and publications, held by one named lead.
- [Evidence Synthesis for Public Health](https://pubrica.com/industries/public-health-agencies/): Systematic, rapid and living reviews, policy evaluation and plain-language summaries built to PRISMA 2020 and GRADE, with the method published.
- [Editorial and Peer Review for Publishers](https://pubrica.com/industries/publishing/): Editorial office, statistical review, COPE-aligned integrity casework, copy editing, metadata and accessibility remediation at portfolio volume.

## Academy
- [Articles for Researchers](https://pubrica.com/academy/articles/): Everything published across the four categories, in one list — newest first, with the category each one sits.
- [Books for Researchers](https://pubrica.com/academy/books/): Longer-form reading: handbooks and primers that go further than an article can, for the topics where a reader needs the whole subject rather than one.
- [Checklists for Researchers](https://pubrica.com/academy/checklists/): Short lists to run before you send something, so nothing important is left to memory at the point it matters.
- [Concepts and Definitions for Researchers](https://pubrica.com/academy/concepts-definitions/): The terms a reviewer will assume you know, each defined at the version in force, with where it came from, what it is for, the variants you will meet and.
- [PICO framework: population, intervention](https://pubrica.com/academy/concepts-definitions/pico-framework/): A four-part structure for turning a clinical or research question into something you can search for, design a study around, and set eligibility criteria.
- [What are the limitations of case studies?](https://pubrica.com/academy/concepts-definitions/what-are-the-limitations-of-case-studies/): A case study examines one person, group or situation in depth, usually from several sources at once.
- [Examples for Researchers](https://pubrica.com/academy/examples/): Annotated real work with the reasoning marked up — the same passage handled well and badly, and what a reviewer sees in.
- [What is experimental research design? Definition](https://pubrica.com/academy/experimental-design/experimental-research-design-definition-types-examples/): An experimental design manipulates something and measures what follows. Random allocation and a control condition are what turn that into evidence of cause,.
- [Types of pre-experimental research design](https://pubrica.com/academy/experimental-design/types-of-pre-experimental-research-design/): Pre-experimental designs have an intervention and a measurement but no control over who gets it. They are quick, cheap and genuinely useful for piloting.
- [Guidelines for Researchers](https://pubrica.com/academy/guidelines/): The reporting standards themselves, summarised in plain language, with the edition in force and the date it was last.
- [Infographics and Downloadables for Researchers](https://pubrica.com/academy/infographics/): One-page visual summaries built to be printed and pinned up, and the data behind each one where somebody wants to check.
- [Journal quartiles explained: Q1 to Q4](https://pubrica.com/academy/journal-selection/journal-quartiles-q1-q2-q3-q4-ranking-guide/): A quartile tells you where a journal sits against others in its subject category on one citation metric. It tells you nothing about whether your paper.
- [Cardiology trial reporting under CONSORT](https://pubrica.com/academy/journal-submission/cardiology-manuscripts-consort-2025-compliance/): CONSORT was updated in 2025, and the revision is not cosmetic.
- [Oncology manuscripts: CONSORT and RECIST](https://pubrica.com/academy/journal-submission/oncology-manuscripts-consort-recist-submission/): Oncology reviewers check response criteria reporting the way cardiology reviewers check registration.
- [Academy Resource Library](https://pubrica.com/academy/library/): Every Academy resource in one searchable library: articles, templates, guidelines, flow charts, checklists, examples, infographics, videos and workshops.
- [What is a literature review in research](https://pubrica.com/academy/literature-review/literature-review-in-research-methodology/): A literature review is not a summary of what has been written. It is an argument about what is known, how well it is known, and what is missing — and.
- [Common types of plagiarism](https://pubrica.com/academy/plagiarism-service/common-types-of-plagiarism/): Most plagiarism in research is not theft. It is a citation that was meant to be added later, a paraphrase that stayed too close, or an author reusing their.
- [Process Flow Charts for Researchers](https://pubrica.com/academy/process-flow-charts/): The sequences drawn out: what happens in what order, who decides at each point, and where a project most often.
- [Ask a Question for Researchers](https://pubrica.com/academy/questions/): A question answered by the subject matter expert who works in that field, published where the answer is useful to more than one.
- [Research Data Analytics and AI](https://pubrica.com/academy/research-data-analytics-ai/): Knowing what the numbers will and will not support: design, analysis, interpretation, reproducibility, and where AI belongs in research work and where it.
- [Research Promotion](https://pubrica.com/academy/research-promotion/): Getting the work read once it is published: congress, visual and video formats, digital profile and the media that reaches beyond the.
- [How to write a research proposal: a complete guide](https://pubrica.com/academy/research-proposal/how-to-write-a-research-proposal-a-complete-guide/): A proposal is judged on how well the study is argued, not on what the study will find. Reviewers are deciding one thing: whether this question is worth.
- [Research Publication](https://pubrica.com/academy/research-publication/): Where to send the work, what the destination requires, and the declarations that have to be right before anybody reads the.
- [Research Writing](https://pubrica.com/academy/research-writing/): Getting the work onto the page so a reviewer can follow it: language, structure, figures, references and the reporting standard your design.
- [Responding to Reviewer Comments: a Point-by-Point](https://pubrica.com/academy/response-to-reviewer/responding-to-reviewer-comments-rebuttal-letter/): How to structure a rebuttal letter an editor can adjudicate quickly: what to concede, what to defend, how to word a disagreement.
- [Templates for Researchers](https://pubrica.com/academy/templates/): Document shells you fill in rather than build from nothing — manuscript structures, checklists, declaration wording and submission.
- [Videos for Researchers](https://pubrica.com/academy/videos/): Short recorded walkthroughs for the things that are quicker to watch once than to read three. This library is being filled rather than finished.
- [Workshops and Webinars for Researchers](https://pubrica.com/academy/workshops/): Live taught sessions for a group, built around your own manuscripts rather than worked examples.

## Insights
- [How to choose an academic publisher](https://pubrica.com/insights/choosing-an-academic-publisher/): For a book or a monograph the publisher decides more than the journal does for an article: the series you sit in, whether libraries buy it, whether it is.
- [How to declare an editor in your acknowledgements](https://pubrica.com/insights/declaring-thesis-editing/): Using an editor is normal and disclosing it is required.
- [Reading a desk rejection properly](https://pubrica.com/insights/desk-rejection-diagnosis/): Four sentences from an editor usually contain the real reason your paper was returned without review.
- [Why figures fail at production, not at review](https://pubrica.com/insights/figures-that-fail-at-production/): A figure that reviewers praised can stop a paper for three weeks after acceptance.
- [Horizon Europe Will Not Pay a Hybrid Journal APC](https://pubrica.com/insights/horizon-europe-article-processing-charges/): Article processing charges are reimbursable only in fully open-access journals. How to comply for nothing, and the statement you need at submission.
- [Writing patient education materials that change](https://pubrica.com/insights/how-physicians-can-write-clear-and-impactful-patient-education-materials/): Most patient materials are accurate, complete and unread. The gap between a leaflet that is correct and one that changes what a patient does is mostly.
- [Choosing a journal for a case report](https://pubrica.com/insights/how-should-physicians-choose-the-right-journal-for-submitting-a-case-report/): Fewer journals publish case reports than a decade ago, and the ones that do have narrowed what they accept. Placing one well is mostly a matter of knowing.
- [Japan’s Immediate Open Access Rule from FY2025](https://pubrica.com/insights/japan-immediate-open-access/): KAKENHI, JST and AMED now require immediate open access with no embargo, reported annually with the DOI. Three routes, two of them free.
- [NIH Public Access Policy 2025: What Changed](https://pubrica.com/insights/nih-public-access-policy-2025/): The twelve-month embargo is gone: since 1 July 2025 the accepted manuscript goes to PubMed Central on acceptance.
- [The same passage, marked both ways](https://pubrica.com/insights/proofreading-vs-copyediting/): Definitions of proofreading and copyediting are easy to read and hard to use, because they describe intent rather than output. One paragraph marked both ways.
- [How to read an editing rate card, including ours](https://pubrica.com/insights/reading-an-editing-rate-card/): Two quotes at the same price per word can differ by a factor of three in what arrives.
- [Answering a statistical objection](https://pubrica.com/insights/response-to-reviewers/): A reviewer doubts your analysis. The answer that works is almost never a better explanation of the analysis you already did — it is the analysis they.
- [A document revised four times has been proofread](https://pubrica.com/insights/revision-damage/): Errors in a final document are rarely the ones that were there at the start. They are made by revision — and the more careful the revision, the more of.
- [What is the purpose and importance of literature](https://pubrica.com/insights/study-guide/what-is-the-purpose-and-importance-of-literature-reviews-in-research/): A literature review earns its place by doing four things no other section can: showing the work is needed, showing it has not been done, showing you know the.
- [Turning a thesis chapter into a journal article](https://pubrica.com/insights/thesis-chapter-to-journal-article/): A chapter argues completeness to an examiner who must be satisfied you did the work. An article argues one finding to a reader who will stop at the first.
- [Why a thesis reads like a thesis](https://pubrica.com/insights/thesis-to-monograph/): Editors and commissioning editors can tell an unrevised thesis from the first page, and it is not the subject or the length that gives it away. It is three.

## Who we help
- [Who We Help](https://pubrica.com/for/): Researchers, students, clinicians, institutions, pharma, device manufacturers, publishers and education providers.
- [For Education and Assessment Providers](https://pubrica.com/for/education/): Curriculum and standards mapping, item writing and review, psychometrics, bias and fairness review.
- [For Pharma and Biotech](https://pubrica.com/for/industry/): Regulatory writing, medical communications, market access and biometrics. Most of what goes wrong in a submission has nothing to do with the molecule.
- [For Medical Device and IVD Manufacturers](https://pubrica.com/for/medical-device/): The technical documentation a notified body assesses — clinical and performance evaluation, PMCF, PMS and PSUR, SSCP, risk management file and GSPR.
- [For Physicians and Clinicians](https://pubrica.com/for/physicians/): Case reports, clinical literature reviews, original research and CME content. The limiting factor is not the writing. It is that you have a clinic tomorrow.
- [For Journals, Publishers and Societies](https://pubrica.com/for/publishers/): Editorial office operations, copy editing at volume, accessibility remediation, production QA and indexing applications.
- [For Academic Researchers](https://pubrica.com/for/researchers/): For researchers and lab groups — editing by subject specialists, statistics that hold up at review. Most desk rejections are not about English.
- [For Students and Early Career Researchers](https://pubrica.com/for/students/): Thesis and dissertation editing inside the IPEd boundary, statistics explained rather than just run, and your first submission handled end to end.
- [For Universities and Research Institutions](https://pubrica.com/for/universities/): Departmental editorial capacity, research training, statistical support and publication throughput.

- [Global Partner Programme](https://pubrica.com/global-partner-program/): Pubrica’s partner programme for universities, publishers, journals and research groups: rates agreed in advance, the same subject-matter experts each time.
- [Scientific Editor Profile](https://pubrica.com/scientific-editor-profile/): What is in a Pubrica editor profile, what each line means, and how to tell whether the editor assigned to your manuscript is the right one.
